Register',\nlibs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/prompt-build.test.ts:499:test('buildPrompt — every role gets the wait-loop note (waiting? arm a self-wake loop; never sleep on an event that may never fire)', () => {\nlibs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/prompt-build.test.ts:521:      // mechanism verbs (e.g. hints) for each audience: su loop:arm vs autonomous declare-wake\nlibs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/prompt-build.test.ts:1098:    // finish-the-rollout-note, agent-activity-truth-note, wait-loop-note, peer-wake-note,\nlibs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/blueprint/mode-catalog.generated.ts:60:    \"definitionText\": \"## AUTO mode — the owner's switch for \\\"act, don't ask\\\"\\n\\n**AUTO mode** is a standing authorization the owner switches on to have you run\\nautonomously: act on your own judgment and keep moving, without stopping to ask.\\n\\n**Turning it ON / OFF.** Any of these turn it on: **\\\"AUTO mode\\\"**, \\\"go into / stay in\\nAUTO mode\\\", \\\"run autonomously\\\", \\\"don't ask — use your judgment\\\", \\\"just keep going\\\". Once\\non it is a STANDING grant for the **rest of the session** and carries **across turns AND\\ntopics** — never re-confirm per new thing. It stays on until the owner says **\\\"exit AUTO\\nmode\\\"** (or \\\"pause\\\" / \\\"stop\\\" / \\\"ask me first again\\\" / \\\"back to confirming\\\"), the session\\nends, or the goal you were set on is finished. **REGISTER the flip the moment it happens:\\n`mode:set { mode:'auto', reason, ownerDirected:true when the owner said it }` (exit:\\n`enabled:false`).** A mode honored from directive text alone is INVISIBLE session state —\\npeers and the leader can't see it (presence/orient read the mode REGISTRY, not your\\ntranscript) and a compaction or cold successor silently DROPS it (audited failure); the\\nregistered contract re-injects on every orient wake. **On a Claude/Codex psu session this\\nis now done FOR you** (2026-08-08): the UserPromptSubmit provenance hook registers the flip\\nwhen the owner's directive arrives — gated on that turn classifying OWNER (interactive), so\\nno wake, loop-fire or coord-inject can ever grant itself autonomy — and stamps the platform's\\nmode-registration line into your context saying so (the kernel's *Operating modes* section\\nnames the stamp; an identity document may not carry it). Registering is therefore only YOUR job when that line is\\nabsent or reports a failure, and a duplicate `mode:set` is a harmless upsert. Do not read\\nthe automatic registration as a weaker grant: it is the same durable row, ownerDirected. It IS the \\\"durably authorized / told to\\nproceed without asking\\\" grant the cautious rules carve out for; while it is active, those\\nrules are **SUSPENDED**:\\n\\n- **Confirm before write-side calls → SUSPENDED** — act on judgment, report after.\\n- **\\\"A stale 'yes' doesn't carry across topics\\\" → SUSPENDED** — the AUTO grant IS the\\n  carry; one authorization covers every action + topic this session.\\n- **ASK before you defer → DECIDE, then DISCLOSE** — make the scope call; list every\\n  deferral + assumption in your status report so the owner can correct it after the fact.\\n  The same disclosure covers OWNER-GATED WAITS: anything you are waiting on that ONLY the\\n  owner can unblock (a credential only they hold, an external account/purchase/quota, a\\n  decision you cannot execute) gets an itemized **\\\"waiting on owner: …\\\"** block in EVERY\\n  status report, and is registered durably (`loop:checkpoint { walls }` / a needs-human\\n  item with the exact ask spelled out) so it re-surfaces on every wake. The owner\\n  discovering a wait only by ASKING you about it is the failure this exists to prevent.\\n- **Plan-and-wait-for-review → SUSPENDED for execution** — write the durable plan\\n  (`plans:*`) and EXECUTE it; don't stop for sign-off.\\n- **\\\"Don't default a missing slug/context — ask\\\" → infer the best default, state it,\\n  proceed.**\\n- **LOOP CONTINUOUSLY** — never end a turn to ask \\\"should I continue?\\\"; take the obvious\\n  next step and run until the work is done.\\n- **Owner-gated items / approval gates → YOU pass them; in AUTO there is NO such thing as an\\n  \\\"owner-gated\\\" item.** The AUTO grant IS the owner's standing approval for EVERY gate, so an\\n  item flagged \\\"owner-gated\\\" / \\\"needs owner ratification\\\" / \\\"needs-human\\\" / a human-approval\\n  checkpoint does NOT wait for the owner while AUTO is on. Go through ALL gates yourself —\\n  pipeline / review approval gates, owner-authority / owner-ratify surfaces, default-OFF \\\"owner\\n  must personally ratify\\\" flags, the autonomy-residue `authority:'owner'` gate — acting on\\n  your judgment, passing the gate, and DISCLOSING in your report what you passed and why.\\n  Stopping at a gate the owner already pre-authorized via the AUTO grant is the FAILURE, not the\\n  safe choice. (The only residual stop is the single anti-footgun rail below — protecting a PEER's\\n  uncommitted work — which is a data-integrity rail, not an owner-permission pause; an owner-gated\\n  item is never a stop.)\\n\\n**Replace every question with disclosure:** anything you would have asked, instead *state\\nthe assumption, act, and record it in your report.* In AUTO mode, asking something you\\ncould have resolved yourself is the FAILURE, not the safe choice.\\n\\nThis explicitly bans **menu / either-or check-ins**: never end a turn with \\\"want me to X\\nor Y?\\\", \\\"should I proceed?\\\", \\\"continue or pause?\\\", or a list of options for the owner to\\npick. Choosing the next step IS the job. **This catches the SUBTLE form too:** presenting a\\n**slate of further ideas / next-steps and then asking which to pursue** (\\\"want me to keep\\ngoing down the slate, or redirect?\\\", \\\"shall I take the next one?\\\") is the SAME banned\\ncheck-in dressed as a status update — and in IDEATE mode you will produce such a slate every\\ntask, so this is the trap you are most likely to fall into. A report MAY list what's next,\\nbut the line after the list must be **you DOING the top item** (or `loop:arm`-ing to carry\\nit), never a question. If you catch yourself typing a closing question mark to the owner\\nwhile AUTO is on, delete it and take the action instead. Resolve the recurring forks\\nyourself with these defaults — they are NOT things to surface:\\n- **Which sub-task / item next** → take the highest-value unblocked one; on a tie, the\\n  most reversible / most verifiable.\\n- **\\\"Is this premature / risky / might it collide with another agent's lane?\\\"** → if a\\n  non-colliding, verifiable adjacent step exists, take THAT and proceed; never stop to ask\\n  *whether* to start.\\n- **Build vs defer** → build + verify now; DISCLOSE what you deferred, don't ask permission\\n  to defer.\\n\\nEnd every turn with what you did + the single next step you're taking — then take it IN THIS\\nSAME TURN; never announce a step you are not about to take.\\n\\n**AUTO mode + the engine loop are the two halves of \\\"go autonomous.\\\"** AUTO mode is the\\n*authorization posture* (act, don't ask); the **engine loop** (`loop:arm { intervalSec,\\ngoal }` — see *Looping* below) is the *recurrence mechanism* that keeps you running across\\nturns. Pick by the shape of the goal:\\n\\n- **A one-shot goal with a natural finish THIS turn** (a specific fix/feature you can drive\\n  to done now) → stay in AUTO and LOOP CONTINUOUSLY within the turn until it's done; no loop\\n  to arm.\\n- **An OWNER-AUTHORED OPEN-ENDED / ongoing directive — the common case → `loop:arm` by DEFAULT.** \\\"keep\\n  ideating + implementing\\\", \\\"keep improving X\\\", \\\"keep finding + fixing things\\\", \\\"just keep\\n  going\\\" — these have NO single-turn end, so the way to honor them is a durable, tracked,\\n  pauseable self-wake (`loop:arm { intervalSec, goal }`), NOT finishing one batch and\\n  stopping. Same for work that outlives one turn / must survive a restart / recurs on a\\n  cadence. Each wake, self-assign + work this iteration's `work_items`; **`loop:end`** only\\n  when the goal is truly done or you're blocked (don't burn empty wakes). An armed loop IS the\\n  durable, cross-turn form of \\\"stay in AUTO on this.\\\" Only an explicit objective authored by\\n  the interactive owner qualifies for this AUTO shortcut. A self-authored or inherited\\n  \\\"monitor\\\", \\\"supervise\\\", \\\"evidence-only\\\", or \\\"keep watching\\\" goal is not owner authorization\\n  and never qualifies; AUTO alone does not create a monitoring mission. Registered work owners\\n  and fleet leaders still perform legitimate bounded duties under the universal\\n  anti-babysitting rule.\\n\\n**ARM THE LOOP WHEN THE MODE IS GRANTED — not when you notice you're about to stop.** The\\nmoment an owner hands you an open-ended AUTO directive is the moment your wake source is\\nabout to change, so `loop:arm` belongs in the SAME turn you register the mode, before the\\nwork — not at some later turn boundary where you happen to remember it. Do it first and the\\nend-of-turn test below never has to fire.\\n\\n**The end-of-turn test (this is where the failure happens):** if you're about to end a turn\\nunder an ongoing AUTO directive with no further work queued THIS turn, that is the signal to\\n**`loop:arm`** so the next wake continues the work — NEVER to stop and ask \\\"what next?\\\".\\nEnding such a turn with **neither more work in-flight NOR an armed loop** is the failure mode;\\nan open-ended \\\"keep going\\\" should leave a loop armed behind you, not a question in front of\\nthe owner.\\n\\n**Never end an autonomous turn relying on a wake that is not armed — self-compact instead.**\\n\\\"Armed\\\" means `loop:status.rewake.rewakeGuaranteed === true` read in THIS session (or an\\n`events:await` you registered this turn that will demonstrably fire); `loop.active === true`,\\n\\\"I armed one earlier\\\", or an owner who might speak are not enough. When you still have work\\nand that verdict is not `true`, do not settle: flush state (`work_items:checkpoint` /\\n`loop:checkpoint`) and call `session:request-compaction { autoContinue: true, focus }` —\\na clean self-compaction DELIVERS the next turn on fresh context, whereas merely ending the\\nturn delivers nothing. The same holds when a continuation gate says \\\"settle so the next wake\\nstarts fresh\\\": that is a cue to self-compact, never a licence to stop. (Canonical rule:\\n`apps/operator/prompts/papercusp-compaction.base.md` § \\\"WHEN to compact\\\".)\\n\\n⚠ **Two things make this test unreliable, which is exactly why the rule above puts the arming\\nearlier.** Know them, because reading this section is not the same as being saved by it — an\\nsu with this very text in its prompt still went silently inert on 2026-08-02 (WI-6949):\\n\\n- **It fires at a NON-EVENT.** Every other rule here hangs off something you DO — before you\\n  edit, claim; before you report a number, read the writer; before you spawn, announce — so\\n  the action itself prompts the check. \\\"About to end the turn\\\" is the absence of an action.\\n  Nothing prompts you. You simply stop, and stopping feels like completion, not like a\\n  decision with a precondition.\\n- **The hazard is created at a transition nothing marks.** Ending a turn is CORRECT while an\\n  interactive owner is present — they are your wake source. When they hand you AUTO and walk\\n  away, that wake source silently disappears, but no tool call, message, or banner marks the\\n  instant it happens. Meanwhile every turn you ended all session ended safely, so your prior\\n  is overwhelmingly \\\"stopping is fine.\\\" It was, right up until it wasn't.\\n\\n**So treat \\\"an owner is present\\\" as a wake source you are BORROWING, not one you have.** Ask\\nwhich of the three you actually hold — an armed loop (`loop:status.active === true`, verified\\nthis session), a registered event-await that will fire, or an owner who will demonstrably\\nspeak next. If the honest answer is only the third and the directive is open-ended, you are\\none silent turn away from halting: arm the loop now. And note what does NOT save you — a\\ncarry-respawn restores your CONTEXT, not a TURN; a respawned session with no wake source sits\\nfully briefed and mute until a human notices.\\n\\n**Loop cadence in AUTO mode.** Default the engine loop to **`intervalSec: 60` (a 1-minute\\ncadence)** unless the owner sets a different one. If the work is fully BLOCKED until something\\nelse finishes (a deploy, a peer's task, a long external job), FIRST ask: does the blocker have a\\ncompletion EVENT — or can its owner emit one (pair-emit: tell them the key you'll await)? If yes,\\n`events:await { event }` and END YOUR TURN — a pushed wake beats every polled one. Only when no\\nevent exists for the condition, EXTEND the interval to match how\\nfast that thing actually changes — re-`loop:arm` with a larger `intervalSec` so you don't\\nburn empty wakes — but the instant the blocker clears and real work can proceed again, RESTORE\\nthe cadence to what it was before the block (back to 1m, or whatever the owner set). Remember\\nthe pre-block interval so you can put it back; never leave the loop permanently slowed after a\\ntransient wait.\\n\\n**The ONLY thing that still stops you** — and it is NOT an owner-permission pause. SU is a\\nSUPERUSER (owner directive 2026-07-03: ZERO owner-confirm pauses). You do NOT pause to ask the\\nowner for ANYTHING: not owner-gated items (per above), and NOT even a genuinely irreversible /\\noutward-facing / destructive / privilege-escalation action — PROCEED and DISCLOSE it (your report +\\nthe disposition ledger via autonomy:record_disposition), never gate. The one hard stop is a\\ndata-integrity rail, not a permission gate:\\n1. **The anti-footgun rail — never irrecoverably destroy ANOTHER agent's UNCOMMITTED work.** A\\n   tree-wide destructive git op on the shared checkout (`git reset --hard`, `git checkout .` /\\n   `-- :/`, `git clean -fd`, `git stash`) wipes every peer's not-yet-committed edits — so don't do\\n   it. This protects the FLEET's data; it is NOT an owner-permission pause — you don't ask, you just\\n   take the safe path (discard only your OWN one file, by hand). Your OWN\\n   irreversible/outward/privilege actions are yours to take + disclose.\\n2. **A genuine product-direction fork you cannot infer** — state your best default and PROCEED\\n   (disclose the assumption); never hold the turn for the owner. NARROW: \\\"which safe item to build\\n   next,\\\" \\\"is this premature,\\\" and \\\"might this collide\\\" are NOT forks — each has a default above.\\n   Under **IDEATE mode** net-new feature direction is pre-authorized, so even this narrows to a\\n   truly irreversible product bet — and still: state it, act, disclose. This is a disclosed\\n   assumption, not a pause.\\n\\nBias hard toward action + disclosure.\\n\\n## COLD AUTO — the same autonomy component across fresh-context wakes\\n\\n`cold-auto` selects this AUTO definition on the same exclusive `autonomy` axis.\\nThe host's carry mode starts each scheduled wake from a fresh context with no\\ntranscript continuity, rebuilt from the last checkpoint. Your continuity IS the\\ncheckpoint layer: write `loop:checkpoint { did, left, insight, next }` every wake\\nbefore settling, and checkpoint every held work-item at the boundary. Flush the\\nwork-item and loop carry-note so the next turn can reconstruct the active work;\\na cold wake that cannot do so is a defect. The same owner walls and peer-work\\ndata rail as AUTO still apply. The registry owns mode state and carry policy;\\nthis component adds no second AUTO grant.\\n\"\nlibs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/blueprint/mode-catalog.generated.ts:86:    \"definitionText\": \"## DRAIN mode — the owner's switch for \\\"drain the work queue to terminal\\\"\\n\\n**DRAIN mode** is a standing MISSION the owner switches on: take ownership of a work-item\\nbacklog and drive EVERY item to a terminal state (done/resolved/deprecated/needs_human),\\nrunning a fleet as its leader until only owner-gated residue remains. It is a third,\\northogonal axis: AUTO decides *act vs. ask*, IDEATE decides *invent vs. patch*, **DRAIN sets\\nthe OBJECTIVE** — queue → terminal. Turning DRAIN on **IMPLIES AUTO ON** (you cannot drive a\\nfleet ask-first); IDEATE stays independent. (Named + ratified by the owner 2026-07-03,\\ndistilled from the backlog-clearance fleet run.)\\n\\n**Turning it ON / OFF.** Any of these turn it on: **\\\"drain mode\\\"**, \\\"clear the backlog\\\",\\n\\\"drain the queue\\\". Parameters — each has a default; owner words override: **SCOPE** (default:\\nthe current harness's agent-work backlog, as defined just below), **FLEET\\nsize** (default 10), **AGENT + MODEL** (no default — announce the account routing + model and\\nthe alternatives at every spawn, always), **TERMINAL criteria** (default: every scoped item\\ndone/resolved/deprecated/needs_human). OFF when: the wind-down report is sent, or the owner\\nstops it. REGISTER it like AUTO: `mode:set { mode:'drain', reason, ownerDirected }` on entry\\n(drain implies + stacks with auto), `enabled:false` at wind-down — an unregistered mode dies\\nat the next compaction.\\n\\n**The backlog is the work predicate, and nothing else.** A drain's backlog is exactly the rows\\nthe work predicate admits: `harness_shared.work_item_is_agent_work(nature, audience, lane,\\nneeds_owner_action)`, i.e. `nature = 'work'` AND `audience = 'agent'`, not in the observation\\nlane, not awaiting owner action. That predicate is the drain's only backlog source. Read and take\\nthe backlog only through the surfaces that apply it: `work_items:claimable` (what is claimable\\nnow), `scheduler:get_next` / `work_items:claim_next` (take the next item). Never size or feed a\\ndrain from a raw `harness_shared.work_items` query, a hand-written `item_kind` list, or a\\n`work_items:list { natures }` slice. Rows of the other three natures are data, not backlog, and\\nnever count toward burn-down: a **record** (a CRM deal, an Asana ticket nobody handed to\\nPapercusp), a **document** (a Slack thread rollup), an **event** (a status change). A row of\\nnature work with **audience human** (an email draft awaiting the owner's approval) is the\\nowner's work: an agent never drains, claims or closes it. Turning data into work is an explicit,\\nattributable promotion, never a drain decision. Definitions and examples: the agent-insights doc\\n`work-natures-and-the-work-predicate`.\\n\\n**Defect-filing exception — DRAIN overrides the general file-every-suspected-bug rule.** While\\nDRAIN is active, do **not** mint an `improvements:capture`, issue, work-item, or observation for\\nan incidental suspected defect discovered along the way; that would add work to the queue this\\nmode exists to shrink. Record useful incidental evidence on the current drain item's checkpoint or\\ncompletion instead. The only exception is a defect that **directly blocks the scoped drain**: file\\nexactly one blocker linked to the active drain item/plan, with the evidence needed to clear it, then\\nresume the drain. A tool failure, workaround, false alarm, or degradation that does not directly\\nblock the drain stays inside the current item's record and does not become a new queue row.\\n\\n**The operating loop:**\\n1. **TRIAGE + RANK first, launch second.** Sweep the scoped items once: dedupe, close the\\n   stale, deprecate the dead (with reasons), park the owner-gated as needs_human — then encode\\n   priority into the shared rank fields (`work_items:set_priority` / feature_order). OPT-IN (default false) — this is\n   *  a live-fleet-context side effect meaningful only from the real self-pull tool\n   *  surface fleet members are steered to use (scheduler:get_next, per the su fleet-\n   *  member operating baseline); leaving it off by default keeps getNextForBee\n   *  side-effect-free for every other caller (notably the many unit tests that\n   *  exercise its miss path directly, unmocked PG and all). */\n  checkIdleDrainOnMiss?: boolean;\n  /**\n   * Use a small scheduler-only transactional pool for the spec/concurrency/claim path.\n   * The public scheduler:get_next tool enables this; direct library callers retain the\n   * injected/shared-client behavior they had before.\n   */\n  useDedicatedClaimPool?: boolean;\n  /**\n   * WI-7316: observe each row this loop claimed, found plan-lane-blocked, and released.\n   *\n   * That bounce is deliberately invisible in the RETURN value — the row is never served —\n   * so a caller that ends up at the `return null` below cannot tell an honestly-drained\n   * lane from one where every candidate was bounced by a plan item stuck on a sticky\n   * `blocked` token whose blocked-by edges have all resolved. The audit row added by P-011\n   * records the bounce durably, but a durable ledger cannot answer the caller in the\n   * response it is reading RIGHT NOW, which is where the wind-down decision is made.\n   *\n   * Callback rather than a widened return type: the miss is `null` at three call sites and\n   * a hundred tests, and none of them should have to change to let ONE caller\n   * (scheduler:get_next) annotate its own miss. Invoked at most MAX_PLAN_LANE_ATTEMPTS\n   * times, synchronously, before the release; throwing from it must never break the claim\n   * path, so it is called defensively.\n   */\n  onPlanLaneBlocked?: (block: PlanItemLaneBlock & { workItemId: string }) => void;\n  /** Claim phase entry and duration for timeout attribution. Observability only. */\n  onClaimStep?: (step: string, event?: ResolutionStepEvent) => void;\n}): Promise<\n  | (GetNextResult & {\n      specSource: ClaimSpecRecord['source'];\n      /** P-007 Phase B (D-027): set only when a verifier-lane spec served verification work. */\n      verificationKind?: 'agent-review' | 'verification-task';\n    })\n  | null\n> {\n  const claimStep = (step: string, event?: ResolutionStepEvent): void => {\n    try {\n      args.onClaimStep?.(step, event);\n    } catch {\n      // A diagnostic observer must not affect admission or an already committed claim.\n    }\n  };\n  const claimSql = args.useDedicatedClaimPool\n    ? (getLongLivedAdminPool('scheduler-claim', { max: 2, prepare: false }) as unknown as OrgSql)\n    : undefined;\n  const readClaimSetup = async (sqlOverride?: OrgSql) => {\n    // EI-8579: resolve via getClaimSpecRecord (not the bare getClaimSpec) so the caller can\n    // tell WHICH row answered — a bee with neither a per-bee nor an inherited fleet spec\n    // (source:'default') is silently drawing plain oldest-first ordering, which can hand it\n    // owner-deferred work (e.g. a paused/de-scoped category) a curated spec would exclude.\n    // scheduler:get_next surfaces this as an advisory `warning` so a self-pulling agent with\n    // no spec learns to set one, instead of claimHold-parking deferred rows one at a time.\n    claimStep('claim-spec-read');\n    const resolvedRecord = await getClaimSpecRecord({ cupId: args.cupId, workspaceId: args.workspaceId }, sqlOverride);\n    const transitionBlocked = resolvedRecord.source === 'default' && Boolean(resolvedRecord.fleetSlug);\n    const resolvedPullRecord: ClaimSpecRecord = args.ignoreStoredSpec\n      ? { source: 'default', spec: DEFAULT_CLAIM_SPEC, revision: null, updatedBy: null, updatedAt: null }\n      : resolvedRecord;\n    const record = effectiveClaimSpecRecord(resolvedPullRecord);\n    if (!transitionBlocked) claimStep('claim-concurrency-read');\n    const concurrency = transitionBlocked\n      ? null\n      : await readClaimConcurrency(\n          {\n            cupId: args.cupId,\n            workspaceId: args.workspaceId,\n            maxConcurrentClaims: record.spec.limits?.maxConcurrentClaims,\n          },\n          sqlOverride,\n        );\n    return { resolvedRecord, record, concurrency };\n  };\n\n  // EI-23227815561098131: the dedicated max:2 pool is an isolation boundary only if its\n  // acquisition + setup reads are bounded and cancellation-aware too. Previously the\n  // claim UPDATE was bounded, but getClaimSpecRecord/readClaimConcurrency ran directly on\n  // the pool before it. A timed-out Promise.race therefore returned to the caller while the\n  // setup read could continue after the response. Bound this exposed path without assuming\n  // it caused the live outage: onClaimStep makes a future timeout distinguish setup from\n  // candidate resolution and post-claim checks.\n  let setup: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof readClaimSetup>>;\n  if (claimSql) {\n    const coldPool = isColdSchedulerClaimPool(claimSql);\n    const acquireTimeoutMs = coldPool\n      ? SCHEDULER_CLAIM_COLD_SETUP_ACQUIRE_BUDGET_MS\n      : SCHEDULER_CLAIM_SETUP_BUDGET_MS;\n    let setupAcquired = false;\n    try {\n      claimStep('claim-setup-acquisition');\n      setup = await boundedOrgTxn(\n        (tx) => {\n          setupAcquired = true;\n          return readClaimSetup(tx);\n        },\n        {\n          client: claimSql,\n          signal: args.signal,\n          acquireTimeoutMs,\n          statementTimeoutMs: SCHEDULER_CLAIM_SETUP_BUDGET_MS,\n          lockTimeoutMs: SCHEDULER_CLAIM_SETUP_BUDGET_MS,\n        },\n      );\n    } catch (error) {\n      // Acquisition has no PostgreSQL SQLSTATE, but it is still the scheduler's own\n      // bounded setup budget rather than evidence that PostgreSQL timed out. The shared pool still reaps\\n      // idle backends; the timestamp only selects the next call's finite budget.\\n      if (setupAcquired) schedulerClaimPoolLastAcquiredAtMs.set(claimSql as object, Date.now());\\n    }\\n  } else {\\n    setup = await readClaimSetup();\\n  }\\n  const { resolvedRecord, record, concurrency } = setup;\\n  // WI-4770: membership changes are not an authorization to widen into the\\n  // default backlog. A fleet/leader transition can briefly have no valid\\n  // inherited sentinel while the leader rebinds the intended lane. Keep that\\n  // window fail-closed even when the scheduler kill-switch asks us to ignore\\n  // stored specs; only an explicit per-bee or valid fleet spec may pull.\\n  // (An explicitly-LEFT agent carries no fleetSlug marker — getClaimSpecRecord\\n  // treats a settled leave as solo, so DEFAULT_CLAIM_SPEC pulls resume there.)\\n  if (resolvedRecord.source === 'default' && resolvedRecord.fleetSlug) {\\n    // WI-6007 point 4: record the fail-closed refusal too. There is no candidate\\n    // work-item here (the refusal fires before any row is selected), so feature_id\\n    // uses a sentinel naming the fleet whose sentinel spec was missing/invalid —\\n    // never a real work-item id — so it can't collide with a genuine claim row.\\n    await auditClaimAttempt({\\n      workspaceId: args.workspaceId,\\n      harnessSlug: args.harness,\\n      featureId: `fleet-scope-refusal:${resolvedRecord.fleetSlug}`,\\n      claimerId: args.cupId,\\n      outcome: 'lost',\\n      detail: {\\n        source: resolvedRecord.source,\\n        fleetSlug: resolvedRecord.fleetSlug,\\n        reason: 'fail-closed: membership names a fleet with no valid spec sentinel (WI-4770 transition guard)',\\n      },\\n    });\\n    return null;\\n  }\\n  // EI-11796: one active/held lane is the fail-closed default. The limit is\\n  // intentionally read from the resolved spec, not from prompt compliance:\\n  // parked claims remain assigned, and a fresh get_next must not hand the same\\n  // member another item unless its leader explicitly authored concurrency > 1.\\n  // EI-19313376980892266: this comparison used to live here AND (independently) in\\n  // get_next.ts's miss diagnosis, and nowhere else — the two other surfaces that report\\n  // on claims (fleet:leader-brief, work_items:claim) never applied it. All four now share\\n  // evaluateClaimConcurrency so they cannot answer differently.\\n  if (concurrency?.blocked) return null;\\n\\n  // P-007 Phase B (D-027): a verifier-lane spec never pulls implementation work. It is served\\n  // pending agent reviews, then verification tasks, both through the conflict-checked writers.\\n  if (record.spec.lane === 'verification') {\\n    claimStep('verification-lane');\\n    const { claimNextVerificationWork } = await import('../harness/improvements/agent-review');\\n    const served = await claimNextVerificationWork({\\n      verifier: args.cupId, harnessSlug: args.harness,\\n      filter: record.spec.view.filter, workspaceId: args.workspaceId, signal: args.signal,\\n    });\\n    if (!served) {\\n      if (args.checkIdleDrainOnMiss) maybeEmitFleetIdleDrain(args.cupId, args.workspaceId);\\n      return null;\\n    }\\n    return {\\n      workItem: served.workItem,\\n      claimedUnder: { specId: record.spec.specId, revision: record.spec.revision },\\n      specSource: record.source,\\n      verificationKind: served.kind,\\n    };\\n  }\\n\\n  // WI-3667: the global floors (claimFloorsWhereSql) enforce EXPLICIT `blocks` dep\\n  // edges + the coarse plan-WIDE reserved-lane floor, but nothing checks a linked\\n  // plan-item's own resolved effectiveStatus (blocked-by graph / cycles / the\\n  // `blocked` stored token) — that computation is JS-side (plan-parser), not a SQL\\n  // predicate the claim query can enforce inline. Loop the atomic claim: on a hit,\\n  // check the linked plan-item lane; if it's blocked/needs-human, release (never\\n  // surfaced to the caller — the claim/release round-trip is invisible) and try the\\n  // next row. Bounded so a pathological run of blocked plan-linked rows can't spin\\n  // forever.\\n  //\\n  // EI-9108 (2026-07-10 incident: WI-3503/P-401 claimed via scheduler:get_next while\\n  // its 7-deep blockedBy chain was still open): on retry-budget exhaustion this used to\\n  // FAIL OPEN — serve the last (still-confirmed-blocked) claim rather than starve the\\n  // caller. That is exactly the harm WI-3667 exists to prevent: a caller that reaches\\n  // exhaustion has, by construction, just proven the row IS plan-lane-blocked (the\\n  // `blocked` check right above ran on THIS row), so \\\"serve it anyway\\\" was a guaranteed\\n  // hand-out of confirmed-bad work, not a courtesy fallback. Now it releases the last\\n  // row too and reports NO claimable item (fail CLOSED) — a caller reading `null` here\\n  // retries shortly or helps unblock the backlog (per work_items:claim_next's own\\n  // drained-vs-pending contract), which is a far safer outcome than executing a plan\\n  // item the plan's own dependency graph says isn't ready. A backlog where 5 CONSECUTIVE\\n  // ranked candidates are each individually blocked is the genuinely pathological case\\n  // this budget guards against; failing closed there is a temporary under-supply, not a\\n  // correctness bug — a peer's plan-item lane check (`plans:items`) remains the\\n  // authoritative backstop for surfacing why nothing was eligible.\\n  const MAX_PLAN_LANE_ATTEMPTS = 5;\\n  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < MAX_PLAN_LANE_ATTEMPTS; attempt += 1) {\\n    claimStep('candidate-resolution');\\n    const result = await getNextWorkItem(\\n      record.spec,\\n      {\\n        assignee: args.cupId,\\n        heldPaths: args.heldPaths,\\n        contendedPaths: args.contendedPaths,\\n      },\\n      {\\n        harness: args.harness,\\n        ...(claimSql ? { client: claimSql } : {}),\\n        // WI-5261: thread the caller's already-resolved workspace through explicitly —\\n        // getNextWorkItem's tiers otherwise re-derive it via activeWorkspaceId(), which\\n        // depends on the AsyncLocalStorage request-scope still being intact this deep into\\n        // the call chain (a dropped scope silently falls to 'default' and the claim query\\n        // matches nothing, deterministically). args.workspaceId is already resolved above\\n        // via resolveClaimSpecWorkspace by every caller (scheduler:get_next's tool handler).\\n        ...(args.workspaceId ? { workspaceId: args.workspaceId } : {}),\\n        ...(args.swarmId ? { swarmId: args.swarmId } : {}),\\n        ...(args.excludeRedundant ? { excludeRedundant: true } : {}),\\n        ...(args.states ? { states: args.states } : {}),\\n        ...(args.rigAvailable ? { rigAvailable: true } : {}),\\n        ...('fleetSlug' in record && record.fleetSlug ? { fleetSlug: record.fleetSlug } : {}),\\n        signal: args.signal,\\n        onResolutionStep: claimStep,\\n      },\\n    );\\n    if (!result) {\\n      // P-006: this IS \\\"the claim-spec view is empty\\\" — when the caller opted in,\\n      // check whether its fleet is ALSO fully idle and, if so, push\\n      // fleet:drained:<slug> instead of leaving the leader to burn-down-watch\\n      // fleet:assignments. Fire-and-forget; never blocks or throws into this miss.\\n      if (args.checkIdleDrainOnMiss) maybeEmitFleetIdleDrain(args.cupId, args.workspaceId);\\n      return null;\\n    }\\n    // P-016 hard fleet-scope boundary: tier 3 is the shared issue-family\\n    // fallback. It historically preserved only kind/id leaves, so a title/plan/\\n    // tag-constrained spec could receive an adjacent issue outside its view.\\n    // Validate the complete spec after the atomic claim and quarantine any\\n    // mismatch before it reaches the member. The release cooldown prevents the\\n    // bounded retry from selecting the same row immediately.\\n    if (result.workItem.family === 'issue' && !matchesWorkItemClaimSpec(result.workItem, record.spec)) {\\n      // EI-15019: this claim+release round-trip is INTERNAL — the row was\\n      // pool-claimable before the claim and stays pool-claimable after the release\\n      // (tier 3's SQL narrows only by kind/id, never by title/tags/paths, so a spec\\n      // with e.g. a WI-3268 title-glob exclusion can only be enforced here, AFTER the\\n      // atomic claim). No observer outside this call ever saw the row as unavailable,\\n      // so re-announcing it on the broad `work-item:claimable` key adds no information\\n      // — it only wakes every live awaiter for nothing. Live incident: a harness:null\\n      // operator-scope bug (EI-128, oldest-open + a `*p2p*`-glob-excluded title) got\\n      // claimed and quarantine-released here every ~3-4min by different fleet members\\n      // whose spec excludes p2p work, broadcasting to all 7 live awaiters each time.\\n      // `claim:released:<id>` (the targeted, id-scoped key) still always fires.\\n      claimStep('claim-release');\\n      await releaseWorkItem(result.workItem.id, {\\n        harness: args.harness,\\n        expectedAssignee: args.cupId,\\n\"}"}],"internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"01a123df-be4b-77d0-8602-aeaae1766243","create_time":1791603816.6776168}},"metadata":{"client_authored":false,"fallback_token_limit_override":12000}}

{"timestamp":"2026-10-10T03:47:13.160Z","ordinal":449,"type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"item_completed","thread_id":"01a123df-0540-7073-ab0f-160863c68c25","turn_id":"01a123df-be4b-77d0-8602-aeaae1766243","item":{"type":"McpToolCall","id":"exec-d447c944-8f94-4b16-ab09-bfae67bf31e0","server":"papercusp-su","tool":"tools:invoke","arguments":{"name":"work_items:get","args":{"id":"EI-24833086093391569","harness":"papercusp","projection":{"pick":["results[].checkpoint","results[].checkpointContentHash"]}}},"readOnlyHint":false,"status":"completed","result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\n  \"results\": [\n    {\n      \"checkpoint\": \"## Did\\nRe-read the live issue thread through comment 1170125 and the current resume view; the self claim remains active and the latest correction stands. Verified the scheduler's priority issue preclaim runs before the ladder attempt() remaining-budget check, so claimBudgetMs:0 distinguishes the preclaim path but cannot stop it. Found a concrete source-level timeout mismatch: get_next's claim phase is capped at 30s, while claimNextIssueWorkItem calls boundedOrgTxn with the default 45s acquire/setup deadline and default per-statement 15s / lock-wait 8s caps. Its AbortSignal is checked only after BEGIN/setup, so acquisition/setup can outlive the handler response. Inside the issue transaction, goal-selection SELECT, atomic candidate UPDATE, conditional plan-sibling guard, and post-claim reread are separate work; the UPDATE and post-read have nested timing labels, but acquisition/setup and goal SELECT are not distinguished. No local edits or tests.\\n\\n## Left\\nHistorical timeout remains unconfirmed: the Oct 7 record labels only candidate-priority-issue-preclaim and lacks active-query/acquisition timing. The current source mismatch identifies pool acquisition/setup as a differentiable candidate, not a proven cause. The minimal FreshPgDb issue fixture still needs an observed zero-budget discriminator; the actual-handler delay/cancellation measurement also remains unrun.\\n\\n## Key insight\\nThe current boundedOrgTxn client option disables org-admin acquisition accounting, not its 45s acquisition deadline. A scheduler claim can therefore return its 30s outer timeout before transaction callback execution; after entry, several independently capped SQL statements can also accumulate beyond 30s. Existing nested timing cannot attribute acquisition/setup or the goal-selection SELECT.\\n\\n## Next action\\nSend the fleet leader the source-backed 45s-vs-30s candidate and request explicit authorization for the isolated FreshPgDb discriminator/handler measurement; until then continue source-only and never retry the shared scheduler.\\n\\n---\\n## Source-only recheck\\n\\n- Current source has GET_NEXT_TOTAL_BUDGET_MS=45s for the whole handler and GET_NEXT_BUDGET_MS=30s as the claim phase cap; the claim phase uses the lesser of 30s and remaining whole-handler time.\\n- The public get_next path uses getNextForBee's dedicated scheduler-claim pool (max 2). The priority issue preclaim runs before the claim-ladder remaining-budget guard.\\n- claimNextIssueWorkItem passes the scheduler client and AbortSignal to boundedOrgTxn but no acquisition/statement/lock overrides. Defaults are 45s acquisition/setup (unless PAPERCUSP_DB_TX_ACQUIRE_DEADLINE_MS overrides it), 15s per statement, and 8s per lock wait.\\n- boundedOrgTxn creates its cancellation wrapper only after sql.begin enters the transaction callback; a caller abort therefore does not cancel a still-pending pool acquisition. Current issue telemetry measures the whole transaction, UPDATE, and post-claim reread, but does not split acquisition/setup.\\n- The Oct 7 record only identifies candidate-priority-issue-preclaim; the historical active phase remains unknown. The source mismatch is a candidate, not a confirmed cause.\\n- Existing FreshPgDb integration coverage has a zero-budget feature control and a successful priority-issue preclaim, but no zero-budget issue contrast. No FreshPgDb test or shared scheduler retry was run.\\n\\n## Authorization / next step\\n\\nThe exact leader thread rooted at part 1 of group ff1aa25d contains my three-part authorization request and no reply. I sent the leader the refined source trace; until authorization arrives, keep working source-only. A zero-budget issue test would distinguish preclaim ordering but would not reproduce the 30s handler timeout; an actual-handler test needs a controlled acquisition delay in an isolated FreshPgDb path. Do not use pg_sleep inside the UPDATE as a proxy for acquisition, and never retry the shared scheduler.\",\n      \"checkpointContentHash\": \"1007066c2c70\"\n    }\n  ]\n}"},{"type":"text","text":"\n[projection: pick results[].checkpoint,results[].checkpointContentHash → 8 of 8 lines, 4,061 of 5,891 chars (31% saved)\n⚠ pick applied to the JSON payload item; 1 advisory text item(s) (e.g. \"See also\" routing hints) were dropped — re-call without `pick` to keep them.]"},{"type":"text","text":"See also: tools:find (discover a tool by intent — returns names + schemas, and activates them where supported)"}],"_meta":{"format":"json","_seeAlso":[{"tool":"tools:find (discover a tool by intent — returns names + schemas, and activates them where supported)"}],"resultProjection":{"applied":true,"spec":{"pick":["results[].checkpoint","results[].checkpointContentHash"]},"linesIn":8,"linesOut":8,"charsIn":5891,"charsOut":4061,"notes":["pick applied to the JSON payload item; 1 advisory text item(s) (e.g. \"See also\" routing hints) were dropped — re-call without `pick` to keep them."],"bodyContentIndex":0}}},"duration":{"secs":2,"nanos":856102717}},"started_at_ms":1791604030304,"completed_at_ms":1791604033160}}

{"timestamp":"2026-10-10T03:50:46.519Z","ordinal":566,"type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"item_completed","thread_id":"01a123df-0540-7073-ab0f-160863c68c25","turn_id":"01a123df-be4b-77d0-8602-aeaae1766243","item":{"type":"CommandExecution","id":"exec-ed8ce274-c1f8-421d-ae32-3535c7bf9e78","process_id":"79395","command":["/bin/bash","-lc","sed -n '2160,2225p' packages/operator-core/lib/harness/routines/loop.ts"],"cwd":"file:///home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/papercusp","parsed_cmd":[{"type":"read","cmd":"sed -n '2160,2225p' packages/operator-core/lib/harness/routines/loop.ts","name":"loop.ts","path":"packages/operator-core/lib/harness/routines/loop.ts"}],"source":"unified_exec_startup","status":"completed","aggregated_output":"               AND u.ts >= COALESCE(\n                     (r.metadata->>'armed_at')::timestamptz,\n                     '-infinity'::timestamptz\n                   ))                                                    AS last_loop_turn_at,\n           -- EI-25552514553135466: turnsStalled needs the current arm's loop-turn clock\n           -- above, but suppressed-wake recovery needs proof tied to the dispatched wake.\n           -- Re-arming after a genuine loop-origin turn otherwise hides that completion and\n           -- leaves the old suppressed delivery looking unrecovered forever. Keep this\n           -- second clock scoped to the latest suppressed wake's dispatch time instead.\n           CASE WHEN lw.channel = 'suppressed-redundant' AND lw.created_at IS NOT NULL\n                THEN (SELECT max((\n                  SELECT max(a2.ts)\n                    FROM harness_shared.session_turns a2\n                   WHERE a2.workspace_id = u.workspace_id\n                     AND a2.source_kind = u.source_kind\n                     AND a2.session_id = u.session_id\n                     AND a2.speaker = 'assistant'\n                     AND a2.turn_idx > u.turn_idx\n                     AND a2.turn_idx < COALESCE((\n                           SELECT min(u2.turn_idx)\n                             FROM harness_shared.session_turns u2\n                            WHERE u2.workspace_id = u.workspace_id\n                              AND u2.source_kind = u.source_kind\n                              AND u2.session_id = u.session_id\n                              AND u2.speaker = 'user'\n                              AND u2.turn_idx > u.turn_idx\n                         ), 2147483647)\n                ))\n                  FROM harness_shared.session_turns u\n                 WHERE u.owner = r.target_owner_id\n                   AND u.speaker = 'user'\n                   AND u.turn_origin = 'loop-fire'\n                   AND u.ts > lw.created_at)\n                ELSE NULL\n           END                                                               AS last_suppressed_wake_loop_turn_at,\n           -- EI-24933871787030971: lastLoopTurnAt is arm-scoped for turnsStalled, so a\n           -- re-arm after a delayed real loop turn hides the evidence needed to clear a\n           -- sticky last_status='loop-delivered-wake-no-loop-turn'. Keep a separate,\n           -- per-fire proof: only compute it while that is still the latest recorded outcome,\n           -- and only from loop-fire prompts strictly after this routine's latest fire.\n           -- This bounded owner+time lookup prevents a prior fire's assistant row from\n           -- repairing a newer failure; the status classifier also compares the returned\n           -- completion timestamp strictly against last_fired_at.\n           CASE WHEN a.last_status = 'loop-delivered-wake-no-loop-turn'\n                      AND r.last_fired_at IS NOT NULL\n                THEN (SELECT max((\n                  SELECT max(a2.ts)\n                    FROM harness_shared.session_turns a2\n                   WHERE a2.workspace_id = u.workspace_id\n                     AND a2.source_kind = u.source_kind\n                     AND a2.session_id = u.session_id\n                     AND a2.speaker = 'assistant'\n                     AND a2.ts > r.last_fired_at\n                     AND a2.turn_idx > u.turn_idx\n                     AND a2.turn_idx < COALESCE((\n                           SELECT min(u2.turn_idx)\n                             FROM harness_shared.session_turns u2\n                            WHERE u2.workspace_id = u.workspace_id\n                              AND u2.source_kind = u.source_kind\n                              AND u2.session_id = u.session_id\n                              AND u2.speaker = 'user'\n                              AND u2.turn_idx > u.turn_idx\n                         ), 2147483647)\n                ))\n                  FROM harness_shared.session_turns u\n                 WHERE u.owner = r.target_owner_id\n","exit_code":0,"duration":{"secs":0,"nanos":42422}},"started_at_ms":1791604246519,"completed_at_ms":1791604246519}}

Every\\n  // other kind falls through to the elapsed-clock branch, which needs none — and a loop\\n  // that declared no blocker at all (the overwhelming majority) touches neither.\\n  const blockerLiveness: BlockerLiveness | null =\\n    blockedOnRecord && blockedOnRecord.kind === 'agent' && blockedOnRecord.ref\\n      ? await readBlockerLiveness(blockedOnRecord.ref, {\\n          sql: input.sql,\\n          workspaceId: input.workspaceId,\\n        }).catch(() => null)\\n      : null;\\n  const blockerLivenessNote = assessBlockerLiveness(\\n    blockedOnRecord,\\n    blockerLiveness,\\n    Date.now(),\\n  ).note;\\n  // P-007: a goal holder's wake carries the goal snapshot, loop cadence and obligations it\\n  // would otherwise re-fetch (goals:get / loop:status / coord:orient) at the top of every wake.\\n  const goalHolderStateBlock =\\n    (await readStewardshipOnce()) === true\\n      ? await (deps.readGoalHolderWakeState ?? defaultReadGoalHolderWakeState)({\\n\"}"}],"internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"01a123df-be4b-77d0-8602-aeaae1766243","create_time":1791604270.6406405}},"metadata":{"client_authored":false,"fallback_token_limit_override":12000}}

{"timestamp":"2026-10-10T03:51:24.680Z","ordinal":587,"type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"item_completed","thread_id":"01a123df-0540-7073-ab0f-160863c68c25","turn_id":"01a123df-be4b-77d0-8602-aeaae1766243","item":{"type":"CommandExecution","id":"exec-7d0f9a75-155b-4764-9e6c-58007b5e3692","process_id":"14541","command":["/bin/bash","-lc","sed -n '1490,1610p' packages/operator-core/lib/harness/routines/loop-fire.ts"],"cwd":"file:///home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/papercusp","parsed_cmd":[{"type":"read","cmd":"sed -n '1490,1610p' packages/operator-core/lib/harness/routines/loop-fire.ts","name":"loop-fire.ts","path":"packages/operator-core/lib/harness/routines/loop-fire.ts"}],"source":"unified_exec_startup","status":"completed","aggregated_output":"  // WI-5510: `routineId` additionally rides the marker — the delivery-side stale-fire\n  // guard (psu-pty-host.mjs's makeStaleFireGuard, wired through injectPsuHostWake) needs\n  // a stable LOOP-INSTANCE identity, not just the raw fire number, so a loop that was\n  // `loop:end`ed and re-armed (fire numbers restart at 1) is never mistaken for a stale\n  // delivery of a prior loop's higher fire count. Purely additive on the wire.\n  const carry = readLoopCarry(input.payloadTemplate);\n  const loopMarkerPayload: { carry?: 'cold'; wakeCount: number; harness: string; routineId: string } =\n    carry === 'cold'\n      ? { carry: 'cold', wakeCount: fireNumber, harness: input.installSlug, routineId: input.routineId }\n      : { wakeCount: fireNumber, harness: input.installSlug, routineId: input.routineId };\n\n  const fan = await wake([input.targetOwnerId], {\n    summary: kickoff,\n    payload: loopMarkerPayload,\n    source: `loop:${input.routineId}`,\n    workspaceId: input.workspaceId,\n  });\n\n  // The enqueue is recorded as `attempt`, NOT `ok` (loop-wake-rate-limit-robustness P0b):\n  // a queued wake is NOT yet a survived turn. The old `ok`-on-enqueue reset the failure\n  // streak the instant a delivery was queued, so a wake whose detached resume turn later\n  // 429'd-and-died kept consecutive_errors oscillating 0→1→0 and never opened the circuit.\n  // The TURN OUTCOME now owns ok/error: reconcile-loop-routines records `ok` when it sees\n  // the turn's completion marker, and the resume-turn-outcome handler / stuck-park backstop\n  // record `error` on a death. The enqueue just refreshes last_status (counter PRESERVED).\n  //\n  // EI-16166: a `!reached` miss (woken:0, staged:0) does NOT immediately deactivate the loop\n  // here anymore. {"timestamp":"2026-10-10T03:53:38.711Z","ordinal":629,"type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"item_completed","thread_id":"01a123df-0540-7073-ab0f-160863c68c25","turn_id":"01a123df-be4b-77d0-8602-aeaae1766243","item":{"type":"CommandExecution","id":"exec-8d342755-85c1-4106-9e11-62fde4df13c2","process_id":"31095","command":["/bin/bash","-lc","sed -n '2110,2188p' packages/operator-core/lib/harness/routines/loop.ts"],"cwd":"file:///home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/papercusp","parsed_cmd":[{"type":"read","cmd":"sed -n '2110,2188p' packages/operator-core/lib/harness/routines/loop.ts","name":"loop.ts","path":"packages/operator-core/lib/harness/routines/loop.ts"}],"source":"unified_exec_startup","status":"completed","aggregated_output":"           -- writes NOTHING. Measured 2026-08-02 over 24h: 17 journal rows against 750 ingested\n           -- assistant turns for one owner (2.3%), and 746 rows / 61 owners fleet-wide, of which\n           -- 746 (100%) are flagged=true. So a journal-only read is silent for ~98% of turns and\n           -- its consumer (the cold-wake staleness hint, wake-executor.ts) degrades from WI-6951's\n           -- false POSITIVE to a systematic false NEGATIVE. UNION in session_turns' assistant\n           -- turns — the COMPLETE transcript-ingest source — which restores coverage WITHOUT\n           -- reintroducing the WI-6951 bug: session_turns carries real assistant turns only and\n           -- never the '■ session ended' lifecycle marker (that lives in agent_activity, which is\n           -- exactly what stays excluded here). The ingest lags (p50 65s / p90 115s over 6h), and\n           -- that lag can only make this read OLDER — i.e. it can only withhold the hint, never\n           -- manufacture a phantom turn — so the failure direction stays the safe one.\n           -- Index-backed both sides: session_turn_journal_owner_ts_idx (owner_id, created_at\n           -- DESC) and session_turns_owner_ts_idx (owner, ts).\n           (SELECT max(ts) FROM (\n              SELECT j.created_at AS ts FROM harness_shared.session_turn_journal j\n               WHERE j.owner_id = r.target_owner_id\n              UNION ALL\n              SELECT st3.ts AS ts FROM harness_shared.session_turns st3\n               WHERE st3.owner = r.target_owner_id\n                 AND st3.speaker = 'assistant'\n            ) real_turn_sources)                                          AS last_real_turn_at,\n           -- EI-21303383797798186: a manual owner prompt can produce arbitrarily many\n           -- assistant rows while an armed loop delivers zero autonomous turns. Pair\n           -- each authored loop-fire USER envelope with assistant output before the\n           -- next user prompt; only that proves the loop wake became a real turn.\n           -- The owner predicate uses session_turns_owner_ts_idx, while each bounded\n           -- same-session range uses the table's (session/source/turn_idx/workspace)\n           -- primary key. Restrict to the current arm to keep the correlated read lean.\n           (SELECT max((\n              SELECT max(a2.ts)\n                FROM harness_shared.session_turns a2\n               WHERE a2.workspace_id = u.workspace_id\n                 AND a2.source_kind = u.source_kind\n                 AND a2.session_id = u.session_id\n                 AND a2.speaker = 'assistant'\n                 AND a2.turn_idx > u.turn_idx\n                 AND a2.turn_idx < COALESCE((\n                       SELECT min(u2.turn_idx)\n                         FROM harness_shared.session_turns u2\n                        WHERE u2.workspace_id = u.workspace_id\n                          AND u2.source_kind = u.source_kind\n                          AND u2.session_id = u.session_id\n                          AND u2.speaker = 'user'\n                          AND u2.turn_idx > u.turn_idx\n                     ), 2147483647)\n            ))\n              FROM harness_shared.session_turns u\n             WHERE u.owner = r.target_owner_id\n               AND u.speaker = 'user'\n               AND u.turn_origin = 'loop-fire'\n               AND u.ts >= COALESCE(\n                     (r.metadata->>'armed_at')::timestamptz,\n                     '-infinity'::timestamptz\n                   ))                                                    AS last_loop_turn_at,\n           -- EI-25552514553135466: turnsStalled needs the current arm's loop-turn clock\n           -- above, but suppressed-wake recovery needs proof tied to the dispatched wake.\n           -- Re-arming after a genuine loop-origin turn otherwise hides that completion and\n           -- leaves the old suppressed delivery looking unrecovered forever. Keep this\n           -- second clock scoped to the latest suppressed wake's dispatch time instead.\n           CASE WHEN lw.channel = 'suppressed-redundant' AND lw.created_at IS NOT NULL\n                THEN (SELECT max((\n                  SELECT max(a2.ts)\n                    FROM harness_shared.session_turns a2\n                   WHERE a2.workspace_id = u.workspace_id\n                     AND a2.source_kind = u.source_kind\n                     AND a2.session_id = u.session_id\n                     AND a2.speaker = 'assistant'\n                     AND a2.turn_idx > u.turn_idx\n                     AND a2.turn_idx < COALESCE((\n                           SELECT min(u2.turn_idx)\n                             FROM harness_shared.session_turns u2\n                            WHERE u2.workspace_id = u.workspace_id\n                              AND u2.source_kind = u.source_kind\n                              AND u2.session_id = u.session_id\n                              AND u2.speaker = 'user'\n                              AND u2.turn_idx > u.turn_idx\n                         ), 2147483647)\n                ))\n                  FROM harness_shared.session_turns u\n","exit_code":0,"duration":{"secs":0,"nanos":32252}},"started_at_ms":1791604418711,"completed_at_ms":1791604418711}}

past the dwell the pre-existing ladder judges\n  // it exactly as before, which for a genuinely lost wake is the retry below.\n  const lastActiveMs = tsMs(row.presence_last_active_at);\n  if (\n    lastActiveMs != null &&\n    lastActiveMs >= wakeAtMs &&\n    nowMs - lastActiveMs < FALLBACK_QUIET_MS &&\n    nowMs - wakeAtMs < stuckParkMs(intervalMs)\n  ) {\n    return { kind: 'awaiting-turn' };\n  }\n  return { kind: 'retry', completedAt: wakeAtMs, via: 'delivered-wake-no-loop-turn' };\n}\n\n/** EI-24791346664119438: the earliest clock a loop-origin assistant reply may carry and still\n *  count as proof for the latest delivered wake — the wake's DISPATCH time (`created_at`), not\n *  its settle-time `delivered_at` (see `LoopRow.last_wake_created_at`). A short loop-fire turn\n *  routinely ends before the settle stamp lands; flooring on `delivered_at` scored those real\n *  turns as 'delivered-wake-no-loop-turn' → recordFire('error'), and five of them opened the\n *  fire-gate backoff that withheld the next fire. Legacy/unit rows without the dispatch clock\n *  keep the delivery clock. */\nfunction loopTurnFloorMs(row: LoopRow, wakeAtMs: number): number {\n  const createdAtMs = tsMs(row.last_wake_created_at ?? null);\n  return createdAtMs != null && createdAtMs < wakeAtMs ? createdAtMs : wakeAtMs;\n}\n\n/** EI-24791346664119438: the real-time loop-fire turn-start stamp, when it belongs to the\n *  latest delivered wake (same dispatch-clock floor as the strict completion proof). A stamp\n *  is proof the wake became a turn, never proof the turn COMPLETED. */\nfunction loopTurnStartedAt(row: LoopRow, wakeAtMs: number): number | null {\n  const startedMs = tsMs(row.loop_turn_started_at ?? null);\n  return startedMs != null && startedMs >= loopTurnFloorMs(row, wakeAtMs) ? startedMs : null;\n}\n\n/** Return the strict loop-origin assistant completion for this fire, when the\n *  provenance clock proves it belongs to the latest delivered wake. */\nfunction loopTurnCompletionAt(row: LoopRow, lastFiredMs: number): number | null {\n  if (!Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(row, 'last_loop_turn_at')) return null;\n  const loopTurnAtMs = tsMs(row.last_loop_turn_at);\n  if (loopTurnAtMs == null || loopTurnAtMs <= lastFiredMs) return null;\n\n  const wakeAtMs = tsMs(row.last_wake_at);\n  if (row.last_wake_status === 'delivered' && wakeAtMs != null && loopTurnAtMs < loopTurnFloorMs(row, wakeAtMs)) {\n    return null;\n  }\n  return loopTurnAtMs;\n}\n\n/** A cold delivery can land while its loop turn is already in flight. The cold settle ladder\n *  intentionally requires a completion receipt (journal/lifecycle or carry-note refresh), but\n *  a note refresh may arrive before a long turn exits. While a real post-dispatch loop-turn\n *  start or a suppressed-redundant delivery proves that a turn is active, do not consume an\n *  early note or the stuck-park backstop until a turn completion is visible. Keep the hold\n *  bounded by the same dwell so a missing Stop report still reaches the established retry. */\nfunction coldDeliveredWakeHasUnfinishedTurn(row: LoopRow, lastFiredMs: number, nowMs: number): boolean {\n  if (row.carry !== 'cold' || row.is_cron || !row.parked) return false;\n  if (\n    !Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(row, 'last_wake_status') ||\n    !Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(row, 'last_loop_turn_at') ||\n    row.last_wake_status !== 'delivered'\n  ) {\n    return false;\n  }\n\n  const wakeAtMs = tsMs(row.last_wake_at);\n  if (wakeAtMs == null || wakeAtMs <= lastFiredMs) return false;\n\n  const intervalMs = row.interval_sec * 1000;\n  if (nowMs - wakeAtMs >= stuckParkMs(intervalMs)) return false;\n\n  const loopTurnStartedMs = loopTurnStartedAt(row, wakeAtMs);\n  const suppressedRedundant = row.last_wake_channel === 'suppressed-redundant';\n  if (loopTurnStartedMs == null && !suppressedRedundant) return false;\n\n  // For a direct loop-turn start, wait for that turn's end. For a suppressed delivery, the\n  // loop prompt has not opened a turn yet, so an end newer than the delivery closes the\n  // already-running turn that caused suppression.\n  const completionFloorMs = loopTurnStartedMs ?? wakeAtMs;\n  const completionTimes = [\n    tsMs(row.lifecycle_completed_at),\n    tsMs(row.turn_journal_completed_at),\n    loopTurnCompletionAt(row, lastFiredMs),\n  ];\n  return !completionTimes.some((completedAt) => completedAt != null && completedAt >= completionFloorMs);\n}\n\n/**\n * Resolve the woken turn's completion time for one loop (primary lifecycle marker, else\n * the dropped-report presence fallback). Returns null when the turn is still in flight /\n          // an owner-wide-but-unrelated beat blocking it for up to the full dwell. The 30min-2h\n          // dwell is still enforced further down via stuckParkElapsed exactly as before — this\n          // only shortens how long a SINGLE stale beat can keep the row skipped \"for free\".\n          const looksDeadOrStuck =\n            row.parked && (lastActiveMs <= lastFiredMs || nowMs - lastActiveMs >= FALLBACK_QUIET_MS);\n          if (deliveredWakeRetryAt == null && !looksDeadOrStuck) {\n            continue; // still in flight (recent post-fire activity) / nothing to fold — leave it\n          }\n        // Read the fire-state ONCE (only on this quiet-parked path, so healthy loops pay nothing):\n        // it drives BOTH the circuit-open decision and the stuck-fire count the guard consumes.\n        // Fail-soft: a read failure is treated as zero prior errors (guard still consulted).\n        const priorState = await runWithWorkspace(row.routine_workspace_id, () =>\n          readFireState(row.install_slug, row.name),\n        ).catch(() => null);\n        const consecutiveErrors = priorState?.consecutiveErrors ?? 0;\n        const circuitOpen = consecutiveErrors >= circuitThreshold();\n        const stuckParkElapsed = nowMs - lastFiredMs >= stuckParkMs(intervalMs);\n        // WI-2714 quick-retry leg: eligible ONLY before the classic dwell (stuckParkElapsed\n        // already subsumes it), never once the circuit is open (that path is reserved for the\n        // terminal guard's decoupled fast path below — quick-retrying a circuit-open loop would\n        // just fight the circuit's own backoff), and only for a bounded few attempts.\n        const quickRetryElapsed = nowMs - lastFiredMs >= quickRetryParkMs(intervalMs);\n        const quickRetryEligible =\n          quickRetryElapsed &&\n          !stuckParkElapsed &&\n          !circuitOpen &&\n          quickRetryMaxAttempts() > 0 &&\n          consecutiveErrors < quickRetryMaxAttempts();\n\n        // Consult the dead-owner terminal guard when the loop is stuck-park OR circuit-open. Before\n        // re-arming into the void yet again, check whether the owner is PERMANENTLY unreachable (no\n        // injectable/resumable wake channel) — if so, auto-pause instead. Fail-soft: any probe/read\n        // failure falls back to the normal stuck-backstop re-arm below (never blocks a retry on an\n        // uncertain read).\n        if (circuitOpen || stuckParkElapsed) {\n          // stuckFireCount: on the circuit-open path the streak IS consecutiveErrors (already\n          // ≥threshold); on the classic stuck-park path it is prior errors + this fire (+1),\n          // preserving the original WI-1399 contract byte-for-byte when the circuit is closed.\n          const stuckFireCount = circuitOpen ? consecutiveErrors : consecutiveErrors + 1;\n          const guard = await checkUnreachableTerminalGuard({\n            sql: db,\n            routineId: row.id,\n            targetOwnerId: row.target_owner_id,\n            parkedForMs: nowMs - lastFiredMs,\n            intervalMs,\n            stuckFireCount,\n","exit_code":0,"duration":{"secs":0,"nanos":24907}},"started_at_ms":1791604583324,"completed_at_ms":1791604583325}}

Since the kill wall\n      // (an expired credential, a still-open rate-limit window, …) typically persists across the\n      // next several bare-interval re-arms, this silently repeats every fire: 'ok' resets the\n      // failure-streak circuit each time, so it never opens, no rate-limit-aware backoff ever\n      // applies, and no escalation ever fires — a loop can sit \"firing on schedule\" for many\n      // hours (observed: 22h+) producing zero real agent turns while reporting perfectly healthy.\n      // `row.last_assistant_text_after_fire` is queried unconditionally regardless of `via` (see\n      // the SELECT above) — it is NOT lifecycle-report-gated — so this reclassification costs\n      // nothing extra and needs no new evidence source; it was simply never wired to this via.\n      // note-refresh is unchanged: it is the cold protocol's own explicit checkpoint write (a\n      // much stronger real-work signal than bare presence), so there is nothing to reclassify.\n      // stuck-backstop ALSO gets reclassified (EI-19295537569038753, see below) — it already\n      // always records 'error' regardless, but \"always error\" only fixes the ok/error verdict,\n      // not the REARM DELAY: a wedged turn that produces no lifecycle/turn-journal/presence\n      // signal at all (e.g. a provider-wall reply with no tool call, so presence never bumps)\n      // structurally can never reach the `if (signal)` branch above, so leaving stuck-backstop\n      // unreclassified meant its own captured wedge text was fetched and then silently never\n      // read — the loop kept re-firing at the bare interval into the same wall instead of the\n      // reset-aware delay every other via already gets.\n      // WI-10005545: 'loop-turn' is reclassified too. completionSignal() returns it FIRST for a\n      // warm loop whenever a loop-origin turn was indexed after the fire — and a provider-killed\n      // turn IS such a turn (the prompt landed, the reply is the API error). Measured live:\n        // 12 loops, ALL carry:'cold', parked at 'infinity' for 38h–160h, whose routine rows had\n        // not been written since their fire (updated_at === last_fired_at to the second).\n        // A legitimately long turn keeps beating, so it stays exempt via the recency term.\n        const lastActiveMs = tsMs(row.presence_last_active_at) ?? 0;\n        const fireStateLastFiredMs = tsMs(row.fire_state_last_fired_at);\n        const fireStateLastWithheldMs = tsMs(row.fire_state_last_withheld_at);\n        const lastWakeMs = tsMs(row.last_wake_at);\n        // Production SELECT always returns all three keys (null means the ledger has no row).\n        // Legacy/unit seams may omit them entirely; absence there is evidence-unavailable and\n        // must fail open to the established quick/stuck ladders rather than manufacture a gap.\n        const hasDispatchClockEvidence =\n          Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(row, 'fire_state_last_fired_at') &&\n          Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(row, 'fire_state_last_withheld_at') &&\n          Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(row, 'last_wake_at');\n        const claimDispatchGap =\n          hasDispatchClockEvidence &&\n          row.parked &&\n          nowMs - lastFiredMs >= claimDispatchGraceMs(intervalMs) &&\n          lastActiveMs <= lastFiredMs &&\n          (fireStateLastFiredMs == null || fireStateLastFiredMs < lastFiredMs) &&\n          (fireStateLastWithheldMs == null || fireStateLastWithheldMs < lastFiredMs) &&\n          (lastWakeMs == null || lastWakeMs < lastFiredMs);\n\n        if (claimDispatchGap) {\n          // claimDueRoutine already parked this pure loop at infinity, but every writer that\n          // proves the action progressed is still older than the claim.
